Title: the future of banned cards - LSJ

Messages.Author: Teeka
Messages.Body:
Sorry if this has already been addressed in the 240+ thread on the new
banned list, couldn't find the energy to go mill through all that.

A while ago, it was proposed to temporarily ban problematic cards, for
an unspecified amount of time, and when a good, thoroughly thought out
fix (i.e. errata) was found, reissuing them. (Granted, folks were
talking about doing this to the entire NoR set, but still).

Is that the idea with the new banned cards? I mean, do you (LSJ and
servants) consider these cards to be dead and buried, or are you going
to work on fixing them so they can one day be used again?

I hope for the latter.

Teeka

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
On Dec 13, 3:05 am, Salem <salem_christ....@hotmail.com> wrote:

> I wonder if people falling into group A or group B has any statistically
> significant correlation with those players who played through the time
> of the 7/7 rulings or not.

As someone who was right in the thick of that, I'm perfectly happy
with whatever is most effective for making the game work better. If
errata accomplishes it, ok then. If banning accomplishes it,
fantastic.

That being said, I'd rather have a small number of bannings than a
large amount of errata, given the choice. I don't know if there is any
connection there at all, but I figure I'd throw it out there.

I'm *totally* ok with cards being banned on an infrequent and laser
guided basis. I find the whole "but I wanna use all the cards I paid
for!" argument to be generally empty, as even in VTES, the main
buisness model for a CCG is "sell lots and lots of cards to people
that they don't use most of as they chase a small number of hard to
get ones", so simply by entering the arena of VTES, you are implicitly
accepting the idea that, like, half the stuff you purchase will never
see play anyway. Then, there are the folks who are all like "But I
paid $20.00 for each of my PTOs! I'm mad! You made me waste my money!"
The secondary market is a gamble. Sometimes you pay a lot of money for
cards that become commons in the next set. Sometimes you pay a lot of
money for cards that become errataed or banned. That is a risk, and
always has been. Consider that before forking over a significant
amount of money for a single card.

-Peter

those reprints are easy to acquire (example: if Embrace was reprinted

someone to acquire, say, 10 of them for a 30 embrace deck. Enough that
they're nearly always going to have one in hand, play, or ash heap, to
check for the updated text).

I don't much like errata, as compared to text migration, though, and
complicated errata is probably better served as banning/rewording.

.com>, Peter D Bakija <pd...@lightlink.com> writes:
>As someone who was right in the thick of that, I'm perfectly happy
>with whatever is most effective for making the game work better. If
>errata accomplishes it, ok then. If banning accomplishes it,
>fantastic.

I'm mostly in line with this. As a general rule:

- if a card needs a root and branch re-write, these days I would usually
tend towards a ban
- if a card can be fixed easily, these days I would tend towards errata
- if a card can be fixed easily but still causes design problems (not
overpowered per se, but outclasses many other potential cards,
makes it hard to create new cards), I'm more flexible.

Back during 6/23 and 7/7, errata was - to me - more important for the
simple reason that the chance of new cards being printed was low. Not
impossible, but WotC were unlikely to invest real money in the game.
Keeping cards and strategies around was important as there were a finite
number of cards, and no new cards.

--
James Coupe

All kidding aside, I'm a bit disappointed in the answer.
I mean, basically you're saying "I'm not going to think about them

solution, I'll be happy to dig them up". Which is different from "I'm

the banned list, because I'm a bit concerned where this is going.

Don't get me wrong, I'm not saying I think you have nothing better to
do, but I'm certain some of us would be happy to volunteer for an
"official" think tank/playtest team dedicated to coming up with the
best fixes for problematic cards. You know, without all the not-always-
so-productive talks we get here (no offence to anyone, just talking
efficiency here).

>I think what LSJ might be trying to say is he's always thinking about
>ways to make the game better, and just because he's banned some cards
>for now, doesn't mean he's not thinking about other options for those
>or other cards into the future.

In particular, I don't think he's waiting for someone else to come up
with a good idea. LSJ is likely to be in a better position to do this
than most others for the simple reason that he knows what's coming in
new expansions, and can create new rules, new card types, new costs, new
mechanics etc. If any of those look appropriate for a banned card, I'm
sure there'd be thoughts about/playtesting a re-print with that text.

Hypothetically, if there was a monster combat card that was evil and
broken, does anyone think LSJ wouldn't have considered making it an Aim
card when he invented Aim cards?

And say, again hypothetically, LSJ invents a type of powerful action
with a new cost... say a cost of removing your top X library cards from
the game, where X was the capacity of the target... would he think about
applying that to PTO, or the pre-change Mind Rape? I'd be very
surprised if he didn't think about such things - even if he decided that
they weren't appropriate after evaluating them.

(If LSJ is thinking about such a cost, my telephone psychic needs a
raise.)
